s1.title: Commission publishes guidelines on the protection of minors

s2.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 on a Single Market For Digital Services (Digital Services Act)

s1: Point 1
On 14 July 2025 the European Commission published guidelines to help online platforms protect minors, under Article 28(4) of the Digital Services Act.
Point 2

The guidelines cover every online platform that is offered to people in the EU and can be used by minors (a service that stores its users' content and shows it to the public), wherever the provider is established, except micro and small enterprises (Article 19).
Point 3
They take a risk-based approach: each platform adopts the measures that fit the risks its own service poses to minors.
Point 4
Review the risks the service poses to minors, and act on the results.
Point 5
Set minors' accounts to the most protective settings by default, so that people they are not connected with cannot see or contact them.
Point 6
Check users' age with age assurance that is accurate, reliable and non-intrusive, without collecting more personal data than the check needs; self-declaration alone is not enough.
Point 7
Give minors' explicit choices priority over behavioural signals in AI-driven recommendations, and let them choose a feed that is not based on profiling.
Point 8
Let minors block and mute any user, and never add them to a group without their explicit consent.
Point 9
Switch off by default design features that drive excessive use, such as streaks, read receipts, autoplay and push alerts.
Point 10
The Commission will review the guidelines within 12 months.
s2: This Section, with the exception of Article 24(3) thereof, shall not apply to providers of online platforms that qualify as micro or small enterprises as defined in Recommendation 2003/361/EC.
Providers of online platforms accessible to minors shall put in place appropriate and proportionate measures to ensure a high level of privacy, safety, and security of minors, on their service.

Providers of online platform shall not present advertisements on their interface based on profiling as defined in Article 4, point (4), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 using personal data of the recipient of the service when they are aware with reasonable certainty that the recipient of the service is a minor.

Compliance with the obligations set out in this Article shall not oblige providers of online platforms to process additional personal data in order to assess whether the recipient of the service is a minor.
The Commission, after consulting the Board, may issue guidelines to assist providers of online platforms in the application of paragraph 1.
